artists.biography:
Super Furry Animals are a Welsh rock band who lean towards psychedelic rock and electronic experimentation. Since their formation in Cardiff, Wales in 1993, the band has consisted of Gruff Rhys (lead vocals, guitar), Huw Bunford (lead guitar, vocals), Guto Pryce (bass guitar), Cian Ciaran (keyboards, synthesisers, various electronics, occasional guitar, vocals) and Dafydd Ieuan (drums, vocals). Actor Rhys Ifans is also a former member.
The band formed in Cardiff after being in various other Welsh bands and techno outfits in the area. Ifans, Ieuan and Pryce had been together since the early 1990s and had toured the north coast of France as a techno group. After Bunford and Ciaran (the latter Ieuan's younger brother) joined, they wrote some songs, and in 1995 signed to Ankst, the Welsh indie label. The band are considered to be part of the renaissance of Welsh music (and art, and literature) in the 1990s: other Welsh bands of the time include the Manic Street Preachers, Catatonia, and Gorky's Zygotic Mynci.
The name of the band came from T-shirts being printed by Rhys' sister. She was making Super Furry Animals T-shirts for the fashion and music collective Acid Casuals (variants of whose name have appeared throughout SFA's career – for example, in their song "The Placid Casual", their record label Placid Casual). The band has also made reference to Blur, Elvis Costello, Collective Soul and Wynton Marsalis as major influences in their work.

perplexity.description:
Rings Around the World is the fifth studio album by Welsh rock band Super Furry Animals, released on July 23, 2001, by Epic Records. Following the band's acclaimed early-2000s output—including the Welsh-language album Mwng—this record marked their first release on a major label after Creation Records' closure. Co-produced with Chris Shaw and backed by Sony's substantial resources, the album represents the band's most ambitious undertaking to that point, featuring 12 tracks across a 52-minute runtime. The production incorporates extensive vocal layering, sampling, and orchestral arrangements, blending alternative rock with pop sensibilities and electronic textures.

The album achieved significant commercial success, reaching number three on the UK Albums Chart, though it was briefly displaced from the top spot by Destiny's Child's Survivor and David Gray's White Ladder. Rings Around the World holds historical distinction as the world's first album to be simultaneously released on both audio CD and DVD formats, with the DVD edition featuring 5.1 surround sound mixing. This technological innovation underscored the band's willingness to experiment beyond conventional album formats during the early digital era.

The record showcases Super Furry Animals' evolution from their earlier pop-rock foundations toward a more expansive, production-heavy sound. While the album's ambitious arrangements and layered compositions demonstrate considerable craft, critical reception proved mixed, with some listeners finding the extended song structures and elaborate production occasionally overwrought. Nevertheless, the album solidified the band's status as innovative Welsh rock artists willing to push commercial and technical boundaries.
